stories.headline: Ukraine Strikes Major Oil Terminal and Naval Base Near St. Petersburg
stories.summary:
Ukraine launched a large-scale drone assault on Russia's second-largest city overnight, striking a major oil terminal in St. Petersburg and a key Russian Baltic Fleet naval base at Kronstadt, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced Saturday. St. Petersburg Governor Aleksandr Beglov confirmed the oil terminal was hit, saying 72 Ukrainian drones were shot down over the city and surrounding Leningrad region, and urged residents to stay indoors. No casualties were reported.

The terminal is described by Ukraine's military as one of Russia's largest, capable of producing 12.5 million tonnes of petroleum products annually. Kyiv says the strikes were aimed at infrastructure generating revenue for Russia's war effort. Ukraine has claimed it has disabled nearly 43 percent of Russia's oil refining capacity through recent strikes — a figure that has not been independently verified.

The attack came as Russia's President Vladimir Putin faces rare domestic criticism over fuel shortages, rising inflation, and mounting military casualties tied to the prolonged conflict. In a separate development Saturday, Ukraine's military denied Russian claims that the key eastern town of Kostyantynivka had fallen to Russian forces, with a military spokesman saying Ukrainian forces retained control though acknowledging small Russian infantry groups had infiltrated combat positions.

The strikes mark a significant escalation in Ukraine's long-range campaign against Russian energy infrastructure, with targets now reaching approximately 850 kilometers from Ukraine's border. Russia had not publicly commented on the Kronstadt naval base claim as of Saturday morning.

stories.headline: Keiko Fujimori Declared Winner of Peru's Presidential Election
stories.summary:
Peru's electoral court has certified right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori as the winner of the country's June 7 presidential runoff, nearly a month after voting took place. Fujimori won with 50.135 percent of the vote compared to 49.865 percent for left-wing candidate Roberto Sánchez — a margin of fewer than 50,000 votes. It is her fourth attempt at the presidency; she will be sworn in on July 28 and will become the nation's ninth president in a decade.

Fujimori, 57, ran on a platform of cracking down on organized crime, which has soared in Peru in recent years, and attracting private investment for economic growth. She leaned on the controversial legacy of her father, former President Alberto Fujimori, who was jailed for crimes against humanity including extrajudicial killings and forced sterilizations during his authoritarian rule.

Sánchez, a former foreign trade minister, has alleged the runoff was "seriously compromised" and cited strong Fujimori support among Peruvians abroad as evidence of irregularities. His party filed an appeal Saturday calling for the result to be nullified, though electoral courts had certified the outcome.

Fujimori's election continues a regional trend: alongside Colombia's newly elected President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella, her win marks a broader rightward shift in Latin American politics, following leaders in El Salvador, Ecuador, and Argentina who have aligned themselves with U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.headline: Iran Offers China and Allies Preferential Terms for Strait of Hormuz Transit
stories.summary:
Iran's ambassador to China said Saturday that Beijing and other nations deemed friendly to Tehran will receive "special considerations" when Iran sets fees for ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement signals a dramatic shift from the pre-war status quo, when vessels passed through the strategically vital waterway without paying any toll.

The Hormuz strait is one of the world's most critical oil chokepoints, through which roughly 20 percent of global petroleum supplies pass. Iran's move to monetize transit access — and to tiered it based on geopolitical alignment — could have significant implications for global energy markets and for nations, including European countries and Japan, that are not among Tehran's preferred partners.

The announcement came as U.S.-Iran talks in Qatar over Hormuz tensions are reported to be continuing. Granting China preferential access could deepen economic ties between Tehran and Beijing while increasing pressure on Western nations dependent on the strait for energy imports.

Details on the structure, timing, or magnitude of proposed fees were not disclosed. The move is likely to draw sharp reactions from the United States and its allies, who have long opposed any Iranian effort to control or restrict commercial traffic through the strait.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV Visits Lampedusa, Calls on Europe to Do More for Migrants
stories.summary:
Pope Leo XIV traveled to the Italian island of Lampedusa on Saturday, visiting graves of migrants who died crossing the Mediterranean and urging European leaders to take greater responsibility for the migration crisis. Speaking at a mass on the island, the pontiff declared that "those who have lost their lives in this sea are victims both of decisions that were made and of decisions that were not made."

Lampedusa, located roughly 90 miles off Tunisia's coast, is a primary entry point for migrants crossing from Africa to Europe and home to an overcrowded reception center. More than 1,400 people have died or gone missing in Mediterranean crossings this year, including 28 children, according to the UN's International Organization for Migration.

The visit comes two weeks after the European Union approved tougher migration rules allowing stricter border controls and broader detention powers — measures that reflect a broader hardening of migration policy across the continent. Pope Leo, who has made support for migrants a central theme of his papacy since taking office in May 2025, called on Europe to develop a "long-term strategic plan" for receiving and integrating migrants while addressing conditions in their countries of origin.

The pope's stance puts him at continuing odds with a number of Western leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump, who have pursued restrictive immigration policies. Supporters of tighter border controls argue that robust enforcement is necessary to manage migration flows and protect national security, while critics say hardened policies leave vulnerable populations in dangerous conditions.

stories.headline: Trump Delivers Politically Charged Independence Day Speech at Mount Rushmore
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump marked America's 250th anniversary with a speech at Mount Rushmore on Friday that began with themes of American exceptionalism before pivoting to sharp partisan warnings, declaring communism a greater threat to the United States than World War I, World War II, Pearl Harbor, or 9/11. The speech drew immediate comparisons to the Red Scare of the 1950s, departing sharply from the traditionally apolitical, unifying tone of Independence Day addresses delivered by past presidents at major national commemorations.

The address came amid a brutal heat wave that forced the temporary closure of the Great American State Fair on the National Mall, canceled Philadelphia's Salute to Independence parade, and disrupted festivities across the eastern United States. Officials urged celebrants to stay hydrated and seek air-conditioned spaces throughout the holiday weekend.

Supporters of the president praised his willingness to name what they see as genuine ideological threats to American freedom, while critics argued the speech exploited a unifying national anniversary for partisan purposes. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist, delivered a counter-address framing America as a nation of contradictions striving toward its founding ideals.

Trump has also drawn attention for his expressed desire to have his likeness added to Mount Rushmore alongside Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt, and Lincoln — a proposal that has generated both enthusiastic support among his backers and sharp opposition from historians and Native American tribes who consider the monument itself contested.

stories.headline: Polish PM Warns of 'Critical' Months Ahead After U.S. Intelligence Reports Russian Plot to Attack Poland
stories.summary:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk issued a public warning Friday that the coming months could be "critical" for Poland and NATO allies in the Baltic region, citing U.S. intelligence reports indicating Russia may be planning an armed provocation on Polish soil. Tusk said Poland was preparing for "various scenarios" and urged citizens not to panic while acknowledging the threats were serious enough to warrant attention.

Polish news outlet Onet reported that sources close to President Karol Nawrocki said Washington had issued multiple specific warnings to Warsaw about a plot targeting Polish infrastructure with missiles, drones, or troops. The purported Russian plan, also reported by Britain's Daily Telegraph, would aim to pressure Ukraine's Western allies into suspending military aid to Kyiv. The White House and State Department did not respond to requests for comment.

The warnings come ahead of a NATO summit in Turkey next week, where Secretary General Mark Rutte is expected to highlight European allies' increased defense spending in response to U.S. pressure. Lithuanian and Latvian intelligence services have separately warned in recent weeks about Russian military provocations in the Baltic region, though analysts note Moscow is more likely to employ hybrid tactics such as drone incursions than a conventional attack.

Tusk told the Financial Times in April that a Russian attack on a NATO member could come within months, and his Deputy Prime Minister Radek Sikorski said in June he could not rule out a Russian "false flag" operation within two years. NATO's Article 5 mutual defense clause means any confirmed armed attack on Poland would obligate all 32 alliance members to respond.

stories.headline: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Marry at Madison Square Garden
stories.summary:
Pop superstar Taylor Swift and NFL tight end Travis Kelce were married Friday at New York's Madison Square Garden, culminating months of intense public speculation about the closely guarded event. The 20,000-seat arena was transformed for the ceremony, though many details — including Swift's Dior wedding gown and the full guest list — remained under wraps as of Friday evening.

The wedding is among the most high-profile celebrity events in recent memory, drawing wall-to-wall media coverage and crowds of fans to the streets surrounding the venue in midtown Manhattan. The couple, who began dating in 2023, have been one of the most scrutinized pairs in American popular culture, with their relationship frequently intersecting with both the NFL season and Swift's record-breaking Eras Tour.

The event drew coverage from virtually every major national outlet. No further details about the ceremony or reception were immediately available as the couple and guests continued private celebrations.

stories.headline: Ukrainian Suspect Sought After Parcel Bomb Injures Sanctioned Billionaire and Family in Monaco
stories.summary:
Monaco authorities are hunting a Ukrainian woman identified as the prime suspect in a parcel bombing Monday evening that left a sanctioned Ukrainian multi-millionaire, his partner, and his 13-year-old son seriously injured. Anastasiia Berezovska, 39, is believed to have left an explosive package in the entrance of an apartment building before fleeing on foot and then driving through Italy to Germany, according to Monaco's deputy prosecutor.

An Interpol Red Notice has been issued for Berezovska, who speaks German and is wanted for attempted murder, placing an explosive device on a public road, and criminal conspiracy. German special forces searched her rented apartment in the Main-Taunus district of Hesse on Thursday, seizing a vehicle she had used, but she remained at large as of Friday.

The reported target, real estate developer Vadym Yermolaiev, 58, has been living in Monaco and is subject to sanctions. Investigators said Berezovska had spent several days surveilling the residence before the attack and was caught on CCTV wearing a dark bucket hat. Authorities are also investigating possible accomplices.

Prince Albert II of Monaco called the incident a "heinous crime." The bombing adds to a pattern of targeted violence connected to Ukrainian and Russian oligarchic networks operating in Western Europe, raising questions about the reach of wartime intelligence and criminal operations into neutral third countries.
